sentence: This project studies the gene networks in blood-forming cells that keep the blood system in a healthy, steady state.
This project uses protein and gene methods to find targets for drugs against a type of myeloid leukemia with poor survival.
This project tries to find out whether blocking a glutamine transporter slows the growth and spread of a childhood tumor called neuroblastoma.
This project studies how a protein unfolding machine changes gene activity in a deadly cancer caused by two joined genes.
This project tries to find out how the pattern of connections between neurons relates to how the brain processes information and forms memories.
This project builds an artificial intelligence model that predicts which colorectal cancer patients will benefit from the drug oxaliplatin.
This project uses CRISPR to make genomic templates for studying how a severe childhood epilepsy develops.
This project studies how a bacterial protein helps E. coil that cause urinary tract infections take up metal.
This project tests whether X-ray dark-field imaging with iron dioxide nanorods can show how blood flows in the carotid arteries.
This project tries to find out why blood stem cells in some bone marrow cavities are protected from inflammation during aging.
This project studies why genetic changes in a heart motor protein gene cause a developmental heart disease called cardiomyopathy.
This project studies how disease-causing bacteria cope with changes in metal nutrients and use a dietary antioxidant and hydrogen sulfide in the infected host.
This project tests whether home-based brain stimulation with somatosensory training eases phantom limb pain, and uses machine learning to predict who responds.
This project finds and describes differences in DNA among cells of different human tissues using long-read sequencing and single cell sequencing.
This project develops a DNA-optical barcoding technology that gathers detailed information from individual cells.
This project tries to find out how feedback loops involving RNA control cell migration during wound healing and regeneration.
This project studies how viruses manipulate ADARs to weaken host defenses and how RNA editing changes immune activation.
This project tests whether wearable accelerometers that track sleep, arm movement and walking can predict worsening disability in people with multiple sclerosis.
This project builds data tools that find overdose hotspots and estimate overdose numbers in near-real-time in Los Angeles County.
